title: Talent Acquisition Technician
raw_text:
8-420T. Military Occupational Specialty 420T—Talent Acquisition Technician (Effective 202710)
   a. Licensing/certification requirement. Talent Acquisition Certification.
   b. Prerequisites. DA PAM 611-21.
   c. MOS 420T. MOS 420T is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOS is any MOS. All enlisted MOS
who can substantiate their qualifications with performance evaluations, awards, and certifications in Talent
Acquisition, Recruiting, Data Analytics, Information Management, Public relations, or Marketing as assessed
through the accession process meets current requirements.
   d. Associated SQI.
        (1) 0--No special qualifications.
        (2) 8--Instructor.
        (3) P--Parachutist.
        (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
        (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
   e. Associated ASI. Refer to table 6-5 for listing of universal ASI’s associated with all warrant officer MOS.
   f. Qualifications.
        (1) WO1/CW2 must--
              (a) Complete the Talent Acquisition Technician Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC).
              (b) Be a U.S. citizen.
              (c) Qualify for a security clearance of SECRET.
              (d) Complete Talent Acquisition Certification.
              (e) Complete the Talent Acquisition Technician WOIC.
        (2) CW3 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(1).
              (b) Complete the Talent Acquisition Technician Warrant Officer Advance Course.
        (3) CW4 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(2).
              (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Staff Course (WOSC).
        (4) CW5 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(3).
              (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Master Course (if required).
   g. Duties.
        (1) WO1/CW2 must--
              (a) Perform basic to intermediate level of data literacy to include the ability to consolidate multiple
data sets using data visualization tools.
              (b) Perform basic level of understanding and ability to utilize Human Resources and USAREC
systems at assigned command level.
              (c) Conduct local marketing analysis.
              (d) Understand marketing plans.
              (e) Develop local marketing strategies.
              (f) Employs advertising and content distribution.
              (g) Conduct contract attribution.
              (h) Conduct targeting.
              (i) Understand how to integrate and the fusion process within the organization.
              (j) Advise command on talent acquisition operations that support current recruiting operations at
assigned command level.
              (k) Analyze processing efficiency data at assigned command level.
              (l) Develop external networks.
       (2) CW3 must--
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(1).
              (b) Performs warrant officer duties at higher command levels.
              (c) Performs Talent Acquisition duties in support of Cadet Command, Innovation organizations and
Regional Marketing Offices.
        (3) CW4 must--
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(2).
              (b) Performs personnel duties within U.S. Army Recruiting Commands and Adjutant General’s
School (AGS).
        (4) CW5 must--
             (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(3).
             (b) Performs personnel duties within U.S. Army Recruiting Command and HQs Department of the
Army G1.
   h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
       (1) A physical demands rating of Moderate (Gold).
       (2) Table 8-420T-1. Physical requirements.
       (3) Qualification scores.
             (a) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) - 0120 cm, seated Power
Throw (PT) - 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036
shuttles in Physical Demand Category in “Moderate” (Gold).
       (4) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels: W2 equals
WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are listed in the following
standards of grade tables:
             (a) Table 8-420T-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
             (b) Table 8-420T-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
